entities.explicit_context: William Johnson is a common English name representing a typical individual in Western society. The name follows standard English naming conventions with given name (William) followed by family name (Johnson), and commonly appears with nickname variations like Will, Bill, and Billy in informal contexts.

She represents the medical community and healthcare sector, where professional titles and honorifics are important for establishing credibility and authority in patient care and medical practice.

entities.name: Leo Tolstoy
entities.explicit_context: Leo Nikolayevich Tolstoy (born 9 September 1828, died 20 November 1910) was a Russian writer and philosopher, regarded as one of the greatest authors of all time. He is best known for his novels War and Peace and Anna Karenina. Tolstoy was a member of the Russian nobility and is considered a master of realistic fiction and one of the world's greatest novelists.

entities.name: Xi Jinping
entities.explicit_context: Xi Jinping (born 15 June 1953) is a Chinese politician who has been serving as the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and President of the People's Republic of China since 2012. He is the paramount leader of China and has been described as the most powerful Chinese leader since Mao Zedong, overseeing China's economic growth and international relations.

entities.name: Linux
entities.explicit_context: Linux is an open-source operating system kernel created by Linus Torvalds in 1991. The Linux kernel is the foundation of many operating systems and is used in servers, supercomputers, embedded systems, and mobile devices. Linux has become one of the most widely used operating system kernels in the world, powering a significant portion of the internet and computing infrastructure.

entities.name: Abdul Rasheed
entities.explicit_context: Abdul Rasheed is a common Arabic name that represents traditional Islamic naming conventions. The name 'Abdul' means 'servant of' in Arabic, and 'Rasheed' means 'rightly guided' or 'wise', making this a meaningful name in Islamic culture that represents devotion and wisdom.

entities.name: Mao Zedong
entities.description: Test case for same name in multiple languages
entities.explicit_context: Mao Zedong (26 December 1893 – 9 September 1976) was a Chinese communist revolutionary who was the founder of the People's Republic of China (PRC) and served as its chairman from 1949 until his death in 1976. He was also the chairman of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and is considered one of the most influential figures of the 20th century, known for his role in the Chinese Revolution and the Cultural Revolution.

entities.name: IBM
entities.explicit_context: International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) is an American multinational technology corporation founded in 1911. The company is known for its computer hardware, software, and services, and has been a major player in the technology industry for over a century, contributing to the development of modern computing and artificial intelligence.

entities.name: Apple Inc
entities.explicit_context: Apple Inc. is an American multinational technology company founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in 1976. The company is known for its consumer electronics, software, and services, including the iPhone, iPad, Mac computers, and various software products, and is one of the world's most valuable companies.

entities.name: Linus Torvalds
entities.explicit_context: Linus Benedict Torvalds (born 28 December 1969) is a Finnish-American software engineer who is the creator and principal developer of the Linux kernel and the distributed version control system Git. He is known for his contributions to open-source software development and is widely recognized as one of the most influential figures in the history of computing.

entities.name: Emmanuel Macron
entities.explicit_context: Emmanuel Jean-Michel Frédéric Macron (born 21 December 1977) is a French politician who has been serving as President of France since 2017. He was previously Minister of the Economy, Industry and Digital Affairs from 2014 to 2016 and founded the centrist political party En Marche! (now Renaissance) in 2016, becoming the youngest president in French history.
